claims.statement: The gating supply-chain scan is decided in pure Python over osv-scanner's `--format json` output, never by the scanner's exit code, because osv-scanner exits 1 on ANY finding and offers no severity flag; `_run` never raises on a non-zero scanner exit and `gate(osv_json)` is the only HIGH decision point, returning every finding id whose max CVSS >= HIGH (7.0).

osv-scanner's `severity[].score` is a CVSS vector string, not a number: `_max_cvss` accepts a numeric score directly, otherwise computes the CVSS v3 base score from the vector via `_cvss3_base` (FIRST.org metric tables; unparseable or CVSS v2 vectors yield None), and falls back to the qualitative `database_specific.severity` label band (`_LABEL_SCORE`, where HIGH maps to 8.0) when no CVSS is parseable.

A HIGH+ (CVSS >= 7.0) finding aborts the online scan with `ScanError` (exit 1 from the CLI), while lower findings are returned as `ScanResult.warnings` and printed without failing; osv-scanner's exit 128 ("no package sources found") becomes its own investigate-warning rather than a pass or a failure, and every scanner invocation in scan.py is bounded at `_TIMEOUT = 300` seconds.

Two complementary per-image scan passes exist: a credentialed in-image scan (`_scan_image_in_container`, running the baked `harnessed-scan` in a throwaway container with token env files injected) that is ADVISORY and never gates, and an online archive scan (`podman save` to a tar, then `run_image_scan_online`) that GATES on HIGH+; `_scan_image` runs both and returns clean only when both are clean.

`harnessed build` is deliberately credential-free (`_build_derived_image` never passes a secret), so snyk and socket — the token-gated scanners — only ever run under the credentialed pass; the derived Dockerfile has had no scan layer at all since the tools/install steps moved out of image layers into per-stack volumes, because that layer scanned an image with no stack content while still printing a green advisory.

`harnessed rescan [image]` re-scans one named image or every image carrying the `harnessed=true` label (set by `_build_derived_image` for exactly this purpose); the image listing goes through `_listing` and is load-bearing because an unanswered listing would print "nothing to rescan", exit 0, and silently skip the whole nightly. `harnessed scan <stack> [harness]` scopes the same `_scan_image` to one stack, fanning out over built harnesses; `build --no-security-scans` (`HARNESSED_NO_SCANS=true`) skips the credentialed pass and `_surface_scan_report` then says nothing was scanned.

The nightly rescan is driven by `systemd/harnessed-rescan.timer` (OnCalendar=daily, Persistent=true) firing `~/.local/bin/harnessed rescan` via a oneshot service; the timer requires `loginctl enable-linger` (the user systemd instance is torn down on logout without it) and network egress to osv.dev at scan time — the online DB is the whole point, since a stale-DB nightly sees nothing new forever.

The scan timeout ladder is deliberately layered: per-scanner 120s (env `HARNESSED_SCAN_TIMEOUT`, `timeout -k 10`), a 900s backstop over the whole scan container, and a 1800s bound on the online archive scan — the online bound is larger AND bounded precisely because nobody watches an unattended hang, which would wedge the timer silently and look exactly like a nightly that keeps finding nothing.

`harnessed-scan` always exits 0 (advisory, never gating) and makes coverage first-class: every scanner announces an attempt to a ledger before running, a manifest line is written only for parseable output, and the summary distinguishes `no-output` (ran, probably broken) from `unrun` (never started — no token, absent binary, timeout, nothing to scan, with the recorded reason); an unrun line beats a bare attempt for the same (tool, source), a pair that both reported and skipped yields only the skip so partial findings never reach the totals, and zero reporting scanners prints NO COVERAGE rather than a reassuring zero.

The in-image osv pass encodes osv-scanner's exit-code contract verified against 2.5.1: 128 ("No package sources found") is recorded as a reasoned skip because falling through would write no manifest line and read as a broken scanner, while 127 deliberately keeps falling through since a broken invocation is what that bucket is for; and any early bail a scanner itself knows about must call `record_skip` before returning, because an attempt with no result and no reason reads as "ran and produced nothing".

The attempts/manifest ledgers are a hand-rolled `|`-separated format with no escaping, parsed by `split("|", 3)`; the bash writer strips `|` from every field at a single choke point (`nosep`) because one scanner label is `recipe: $(basename …)` — a directory name a recipe controls — and the Python parser deliberately does not depend on that guarantee, with maxsplit=3 keeping the whole tail as the reason.

Advisories with no patched release anywhere upstream are ACKNOWLEDGED, not suppressed: the list is keyed by advisory ID (self-expiring — a fixed release stops emitting the id) with the package name as a second necessary condition that can only narrow, never a package-name key; every hit is counted, printed by name, and written to scan-report.json while being excluded from the totals.

Scanner output is untrusted third-party input reaching a build console and scan-report.json, so the summarizer sanitizes at both sinks (printable-filtered, length-bounded package names and advisory ids), handles snyk's `identifiers` defensively against non-list JSON shapes, and counts an id-less finding under a synthetic key rather than dropping it (a silent under-count is the one failure direction a security scan must never take) — because the surrounding bash runs `set -uo pipefail` without `-e`, a Python exception would leave the script exiting 0 with no report at all.

Scanner tokens are env-only (never a build-arg, so never baked into image history) and resolved on the HOST from the user-global `~/.config/harnessed/.env.schema` via varlock or a bare `.env` (`_resolve_launch_secrets(project_path=None)`), handed to podman as a mode-0600 temp `--env-file` unlinked afterwards; varlock never runs in-container, project env is deliberately not layered in, a tokenless run explicitly says snyk and socket sat out, and socket derives its org slug from the token (an explicit `SOCKET_CLI_ORG_SLUG` wins) since a container has no ~/.config/socket.

The launcher surfaces the CREDENTIALED scan report as authoritative (`keep_existing`): overwriting it with the image-baked, credential-free report would replace snyk/socket findings with a report that structurally cannot contain them — the exact failure that once produced a green "no high/critical" verdict on a build that had just reported 4 high; the credentialed scan container is therefore kept just long enough to `cp` the report out rather than run with `--rm`, and the build unlinks any previous scan-report.json before the re-scan so an old report cannot pass for this scan's output.

The base image bakes the four scanners plus the scan script once (`mise use -g uv osv-scanner`, `uv tool install pip-audit`, `pnpm add -g snyk socket`), COPYing `catalog/base/harnessed-scan` to `/usr/local/bin/harnessed-scan`, so `rescan` needs no network install and the advisory in-image scan always has its tools available.

The gating online archive scan is executed HOST-side: `_scan_image` runs `podman save` and then a host subprocess `sys.executable -m harnessed.cli scan-image-online <tar>` (the tar unlinked in a `finally`) — deliberately never `uv run --no-project` with a `PYTHONPATH=<root>/src` checkout layout, which died in every installed copy with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'harnessed'` while passing on developer machines because `--no-project` borrows an activated virtualenv (#460, #493). No daemon-in-container and no API socket — the throwaway container the credentialed advisory pass creates is the only container involved in a rescan, and no scanner token is ever resolved from inside an image layer.

The build's post-build credentialed scan mounts the per-stack volumes into the scan container (`extra_args`, with `_ensure_stack_volumes` populating them BEFORE the scan and before the settings merge), so the report covers what launch actually installs — an image-only scan would still pass and still print green while silently covering less — while `_scan_image` (the `rescan`/`scan` path) calls the same `_scan_image_in_container` with no mounts, because an arbitrary image has no stack volumes to mount.

Only the online osv-scanner archive scan can abort anything: pip-audit's JSON has no severity field at all, so its findings are reported as `unknown` severity inside the always-exit-0 advisory summary and never reach `gate()` — the CVSS >= HIGH decision exists only in scan.py's Python gate over osv-scanner's `--format json` output.

Every catalog download surface is closed by a fail-fast pin gate: schema rejects unpinned or @latest entries in recipe `tools:` and in extra-tools.txt, and the base build's staged context raises PinValidationError on the HOST (naming the user's ~/.config/harnessed/extra-tools.txt and the recovery) before podman is invoked — previously an unpinned entry died as an unnamed `exit status 123` inside a RUN layer.

The extra-tools validator must agree byte-for-byte with the build's shell pipeline (`grep -v` comment/blank + `awk '{print $1}'`), which the tests enforce by extracting that pipeline from the real Dockerfile and running it; where Python and awk cannot agree — line separators Python honours and awk does not (U+2028, \x0b, …) — the parser refuses the file (printable-ASCII rule) rather than letting a check pass while the build installs a different tool name, and CRLF/BOM handling is pinned so no carriage return or BOM reaches mise.

The regression gate on the shipped extra-tools template asserts dua's presence and pinned-ness but never a literal version number — an early literal assertion turned red on a routine version bump with nothing wrong — and `parse_extra_tools` rejecting any floating entry already proves the whole file is pinned.

mise ENFORCES the lockfile (a wrong checksum fails `mise install`, exit 1) but only reads a file named exactly `mise.lock` in $MISE_CONFIG_DIR — `config.lock`/`config.toml.lock` spellings are silently ignored and install exits 0 unverified — which is why both install paths set MISE_CONFIG_DIR explicitly and the wiring test asserts the exact filename.

toollock merges per-recipe mise.lock files verbatim (contiguous per-tool blocks, quoted and bare tool paths, TOML-validity gate before merge): identical blocks for the same spec merge to one entry, differing blocks raise ToolLockError naming both recipes and exit the install 1 (fail closed), and an empty merged body REMOVES a stale stack lockfile rather than leaving it to verify a tool set the stack no longer has; a recipe shipping no lockfile is not an error, so enforcement is incremental per tool.

The merged lockfile reaches BOTH install paths before mise runs: the container path passes it as env HARNESSED_TOOL_LOCK and printf's it into $MISE_CONFIG_DIR/mise.lock in the same shell as `mise use -g && mise install` (ephemeral config dir — only the installed tools persist), and the host path writes/removes it via toollock.write_stack_lock into the redirected config dir before the install.

The base image pins everything it bakes: the core runtimes via `mise use -g` (node@22, pnpm@11, python@3.12, …), the node-bundled npm self-upgraded to a patched npm@11.18.0 (the only way to move what the scan sees under lib/node_modules), socket@1.1.143 and @drmikecrowe/hatago-mcp-hub@0.1.2 via pnpm, and corepack deleted with fail-closed proof of removal (resolve `mise where node@22`, refuse an empty answer, assert `! command -v corepack`) because rm -rf on a missing path returns 0.

`harnessed update` classifies pins as resolvable (backend registry lookup, version split at the last @, numeric ordering so a bump is never a downgrade), opaque (install.cache keys, shell SHAs, Dockerfile ARGs — REPORTED, never silently skipped, and never auto-rewritten), or held (hold markers — listed informationally, never offered for bumping, never failing --check); resolver failures and unknown packages are unresolved, never current.

`harnessed update --check` is write-free CI mode: it exits non-zero on a stale pin (extra-tools pins included) but leaves the catalog byte-identical, and unresolved pins alone do not fail it; because it resolves LIVE registries, the pin-check workflow runs on schedule and workflow_dispatch only and must never be triggered by pull_request/push — a third-party release would otherwise fail an unrelated PR its author cannot fix.

On accept, `apply` rewrites the pin in place with a one-line diff: recipe YAML goes through a ruamel round-trip preserving comments and reflowing nothing, extra-tools goes through a line rewriter that preserves trailing comments, blank lines and neighbouring entries and does not match shared-prefix neighbours or the same text in comments; a recipe shipping a mise.lock is relocked in the same write, because a bumped pin beside a stale lock forces mise's provenance-downgrade migration on machines that bumped nothing.

Pin hygiene is lint-enforced over the real catalog as one-pin-one-place: an install.sh shell literal repeating a version the recipe's `tools:` already pins fails the lint (comments do not fail builds), with an exemption allowlist asserted to name only recipes that still duplicate.

Even live-contract test fixtures pin their images (alpine:3.20, "Pinned — project hygiene forbids a floating tag"), because those tests assert external output formats and a floating tag would let the thing under test change out from under the assertion.

`harnessed update` gates offered bumps on a minimum release age modelled on pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge`: `DEFAULT_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_MINUTES = 10080` (7 days, measured 2026-07-25 when all five offered pins were younger than a week). A too-fresh newest release does not mean "no update" — the newest release that IS old enough is offered and the skipped newer one is named (`skipped_newer`); pins whose only newer candidates are too fresh land in a separate `cooling` bucket that `apply` refuses even if passed the wrong bucket, and a newer release with no publish date is classified `unresolved` ("review it by hand") because its age cannot be checked.

The update sweep covers four sources on one classification path (same cooldown, hold semantics, and buckets, so no pin is reported differently): recipe `tools:`, agent manifests (`agent.yaml` pins live in `build_args.<KEY>.value`; A7 — agents used not to be swept at all, which is how three agents reached main with unpinned downloads), the TRACKED template `catalog/base/extra-tools.default.txt` (never the user's host `~/.config/harnessed/extra-tools.txt` — a bump must land as a reviewable diff; an unpinned entry is skipped entry-by-entry so one bad line cannot blind `--check` to the rest), and a declared `unpinnable` backend sorted into its own bucket before the resolvable check so "cannot be pinned" is never misread as a resolver failure.

`apply` dispatches each bump to a rewriter chosen by where the version lives, as an allow-list rather than an else-branch: field-valued pins (anything with a `pin.key` in `agent.yaml` or `recipe.yaml`) are dispatched first to their own round-tripping rewriter (`_rewrite_agent_build_arg` for agent `build_args`, `_rewrite_install_ref` for `install.refs.<key>.ref`); among spec-string pins, `.yaml/.yml` goes to the ruamel round-tripper, `extra-tools*` to the plain-text line rewriter, anything else skipped. A pin kind without a rewriter yields a bump that is offered, accepted, reported successful, and never written — exactly how both field pin kinds were originally missed. All YAML rewriters use width 4096 and indent(sequence=4, offset=2) so a bump is a one-line diff, and `_match_v_prefix` rewrites `latest` to the pin's own `v`-prefix convention.

When `apply` writes bumps, the launcher prints a verify-before-commit block (bd harnessed-czo): the bumped recipes, the affected stacks via `update.affected_stacks` (stack manifests list their recipes flatly, so this is a lookup; a stack with no declared `harnesses:` still gets a line with a `<harness>` placeholder), and the literal per-harness command `harnessed build <stack> <harness> && harnessed test <stack> <harness>` — because a bumped pin is a code change and an unverified bump is worse than a stale one.

Relocking after a bump runs `mise lock` against a COPY of the lockfile in a temp dir (because `mise lock` writes into its config root and a crash must not leave a stray `mise.toml` in `catalog/`, which ships inside the wheel) on a 900s budget (it downloads each platform's artifact to verify provenance), and relocks are collected in a set and executed only after the bump loop, once per manifest against the finished recipe — regenerating inside the loop would relock against half-bumped YAML and discard the work on the next entry.

`_rewrite_agent_build_arg` validates the incoming value with `_require_immutable_build_arg` before writing: a resolver answer that is not an immutable version (e.g. the channel "nightly") is declined by returning False rather than persisted, so the manifest never fails at the next build's schema gate; the refusal is indistinguishable to the caller from an absent key.

The pin-check workflow (.github/workflows/pin-check.yml) runs only on schedule (weekly, Mondays 06:00 UTC) and workflow_dispatch — never on a PR/diff trigger, because `harnessed update --check` resolves live registries — and its check step invokes `harnessed update --check --fail-on major`, so the scheduled run fails only when a stale, unheld, resolvable, past-cooldown pin's offered bump crosses a major version boundary (Report.check_exit_code / is_major_bump); minor/patch drift is reported but not failing, and "any" stays the default for interactive use.

The pin-check runner installs mise (jdx/mise-action, install: false) before the check, because backend-less `tools:` entries resolve through `mise registry` to dated GitHub releases; without mise those pins degrade to unresolved, shrinking the sweep's coverage.

catalog/recipes/tokensave/mise.lock pins github:aovestdipaperino/tokensave@7.12.1 with per-platform sha256 checksums and download URLs across linux-arm64/musl, linux-x64/musl, macos-arm64, and windows-x64 platforms.
